title: Causal relationship between gut microbiota and ageing: A multi-omics Mendelian randomization study.

evidence_spans.quote: RESULTS MR analysis of 207 microbial taxa and seven aging phenotypes revealed 44 causal relationships
examined in Caenorhabditis elegans
explore the causal relationship between gut microbiota and aging
treatment with Akkermansia muciniphila significantly extended lifespan
relationship between Akkermansia muciniphila and inflammation-related proteins and metabolites was further investigated

scope_reviewer.concise_rationale: This empirical biological study analyzes aging and applies a microbial treatment to alter aging phenotypes; it uses distinct genomic, microbiomic, proteomic, and metabolomic layers.

causal_design_reviewer.outcome: Seven aging-related phenotypes, including mvAge, appendicular lean mass, and grip strength
causal_design_reviewer.estimand_or_contrast: Bidirectional causal relationships between gut microbiota and aging-related phenotypes

evidence_spans.quote: MR analysis of 207 microbial taxa and seven aging phenotypes revealed 44 causal relationships
This study aimed to use bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR) analysis
A multi-omics Mendelian randomization study.
Summary statistics from genome-wide association studies (GWAS) on gut microbiota and seven aging-related phenotypes were employed for TSMR analysis.
Akkermansia muciniphila was found to be causally linked
including mvAge, appendicular lean mass, and grip strength
Reverse Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was performed to assess the potential for reverse causality.

causal_design_reviewer.concise_rationale: The report applies bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization to estimate directional gut-microbiota–aging relationships; this has precedence over the secondary C. elegans treatment experiment.
